analysis: In the immune system, cytotoxic T-cells typically require MHC class I molecules to recognize and kill target cells. When tumor cells downregulate MHC class I expression, they become less visible to cytotoxic T-cells. However, natural killer (NK) cells are designed to detect and respond to cells with low or absent MHC class I expression. This is because NK cells have inhibitory receptors that recognize MHC class I molecules, and when these molecules are absent or reduced, the inhibitory signal is lost, allowing NK cells to become activated and kill the target cells. Therefore, in the context of decreased MHC class I expression on tumor cells, NK cells are the most capable of killing these cells. This aligns with standard medical knowledge and consensus.
